title: The Rationals Are Not a Gδ, and No Function Is Continuous Exactly at ℚ
description: Turns the Baire meagre/residual dichotomy into a Gδ obstruction: the rationals ℚ ⊆ ℝ are not a Gδ set (a dense Gδ would be residual, hence non-meagre, but ℚ is meagre as a countable union of nowhere-dense singletons). Combined with Mathlib's IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt — the continuity set of any function is a Gδ — this yields the classical capstone discussed alongside Thomae's function: no f : ℝ → ℝ is continuous at every rational and discontinuous at every irrational. The obstruction is one-sided: the irrationals ARE a Gδ, so the irrational side is not ruled out.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: not_isGδ_rationals: the rationals ℚ ⊆ ℝ are NOT a Gδ set. The standard countable-dense argument, assembled from Mathlib primitives: ℚ is dense, so a Gδ presentation would make it residual hence non-meagre (not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense), contradicting its meagreness.
isMeagre_rationals: ℚ is meagre in ℝ, written as the countable union ⋃ q, {(q : ℝ)} of nowhere-dense singletons (isMeagre_iUnion).
isMeagre_singleton_real: every real singleton is meagre — closed with empty interior (interior_singleton, since ℝ has no isolated points), hence nowhere dense.
IsNowhereDense.isMeagre: a reusable bridge that any single nowhere-dense set is meagre (a one-element countable union), via isMeagre_iff_countable_union_isNowhereDense.
continuitySet_ne_rationals: the capstone — for every f : ℝ → ℝ the continuity set {x | ContinuousAt f x} is never equal to ℚ, because that set is always a Gδ (IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt) and ℚ is not.
no_function_continuous_exactly_at_rationals: the 'no such function' restatement — there is no f : ℝ → ℝ with ContinuousAt f x ↔ x rational, i.e. continuous exactly at the rationals.

irrationals_isGδ_no_obstruction: records the sharp asymmetry — the irrationals are a Gδ (IsGδ.setOf_irrational) while the rationals are not, so only the rational side carries a Gδ obstruction (Thomae's function lives on the irrational side).
prerequisites: IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt (Mathlib.Topology.GDelta.MetrizableSpace): for any f : X → Y with Y pseudo-metrizable, the set of continuity points {x | ContinuousAt f x} is a Gδ.
not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense (Mathlib.Topology.Baire.Lemmas): in a Baire space a dense Gδ set is residual, hence not meagre.
isMeagre_iUnion and isMeagre_iff_countable_union_isNowhereDense (Mathlib.Topology.GDelta.Basic): meagreness is closed under countable unions and characterised via nowhere-dense sets.
interior_singleton (Mathlib.Topology.ClusterPt) with NeBot (𝓝[≠] x): singletons have empty interior in a space with no isolated points; ℝ is a PerfectSpace.
Rat.denseRange_cast (Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Order.Archimedean): the coercion ℚ → ℝ has dense range.
IsGδ.setOf_irrational (Mathlib.Topology.Instances.Irrational): the irrationals are a Gδ set.

mathlibDependencies.description: The set of points of continuity of any function into a (pseudo)metrizable space is a Gδ. The deep analytic ingredient of the capstone; this entry glues it to the not-Gδ-ness of ℚ.
A dense Gδ set in a Baire space is residual, hence not meagre. Supplies the contradiction that proves ℚ is not a Gδ.
Countable unions of meagre sets are meagre, and meagreness is the countable-union-of-nowhere-dense characterisation; used to show ℚ is meagre and that a single nowhere-dense set is meagre.
interior {x} = ∅ when 𝓝[≠] x is nontrivial; ℝ is a PerfectSpace (T1 + connected + nontrivial) so every singleton has empty interior and is nowhere dense.
ℚ → ℝ has dense range (so ℚ is dense), and the irrationals are a Gδ — giving both the density needed for the obstruction and the contrasting irrational side.

openQuestions.question: Construct Thomae's (popcorn) function explicitly and prove it is continuous exactly at the irrationals, realising the Gδ set {x | Irrational x} as an actual continuity set and showing the asymmetry recorded here is tight.
Generalise the obstruction: in any Baire space with no isolated points, a countable dense set is never a Gδ, hence is never the continuity set of a function into a metrizable space.

crossReferences.description: The parent entry derives the uncountability of a complete metric space with no isolated points via the meagre/residual dichotomy; this child reuses the same dichotomy as a Gδ obstruction on ℚ and applies it to continuity sets of functions.
Sibling OQ-01-OQ-02 turns the dichotomy into a cardinality floor (𝔠 ≤ #α); this entry turns the same dichotomy into a Gδ obstruction and its function-theoretic consequence.

Records the dual fact that the algebraic reals are not a Gδ (the transcendentals being a dense Gδ), the same countable-set mechanism; that ℚ is not a Gδ is the textbook special case, and the new content here is the continuity-set capstone.

references.description: Source of IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt, the statement that continuity sets are Gδ, assembled here with Baire-category obstructions.

overview.historicalContext: Two classical facts of real analysis meet here. First, the set of points at which an arbitrary function is continuous is always a Gδ — a countable intersection of open sets — provable through the oscillation of the function. Second, by Baire category the rationals ℚ, though a countable intersection would make them residual, are too 'small' (meagre) to be a dense Gδ, so ℚ is not a Gδ at all. Together they give a famous impossibility: there is no function on the line that is continuous precisely at the rational points. The companion phenomenon is positive — Thomae's 'popcorn' function is continuous precisely at the irrationals, which is consistent because the irrationals DO form a Gδ. The parent gallery entry used the meagre/residual dichotomy to prove uncountability; this entry deploys the same dichotomy as a Gδ obstruction.
overview.problemStatement: Show that the rationals ℚ ⊆ ℝ are not a Gδ set, and deduce that for no function f : ℝ → ℝ is the set of continuity points {x | ContinuousAt f x} equal to ℚ — i.e. no function is continuous at every rational and discontinuous at every irrational. Contrast with the irrationals, which are a Gδ.
overview.proofStrategy: ℚ is realised as range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ); it is dense (Rat.denseRange_cast) and meagre, being the countable union ⋃ q, {(q : ℝ)} of singletons, each nowhere dense because closed with empty interior (interior_singleton, valid since ℝ has no isolated points). A reusable lemma IsNowhereDense.isMeagre turns nowhere-dense singletons into meagre sets, and isMeagre_iUnion assembles the countable union. If ℚ were a Gδ, then being dense it would be residual and so not meagre (not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense) — a contradiction; hence not_isGδ_rationals. The capstone follows: IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt makes {x | ContinuousAt f x} a Gδ for every f, so it cannot equal the non-Gδ set ℚ (continuitySet_ne_rationals), restated as no_function_continuous_exactly_at_rationals. The asymmetry is recorded by pairing this with IsGδ.setOf_irrational.
keyInsights: The whole impossibility is a clash of two structural facts, neither of which mentions a specific function: continuity sets are always Gδ, and ℚ is never Gδ. No oscillation estimate or explicit function is needed once both are in hand.

ℚ fails to be Gδ for a soft Baire-category reason, not a cardinality reason: it is meagre yet dense, and in a Baire space dense Gδ sets are residual, the opposite of meagre. The same dichotomy underlies the parent's uncountability proof.

Meagreness of ℚ reduces to a single local fact about ℝ: points are not isolated, so each singleton has empty interior and is nowhere dense. Drop 'no isolated points' (e.g. in a discrete space) and ℚ-like sets can be open, breaking everything.

The obstruction is strictly one-sided. The irrationals are a Gδ (IsGδ.setOf_irrational), so they are not ruled out as a continuity set — and indeed Thomae's function realises them. Only the rational side is impossible.

Delegating the deep half to Mathlib (IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt) keeps the entry short: the mathematical work that remains is the clean assembly of the Baire obstruction on ℚ and the one-line gluing step.

sections.mathContext: ℚ as range of the cast; Irrational x is by definition x ∉ range (↑), so the rationals are exactly the non-irrationals.

sections.title: Nowhere-Dense Singletons and Meagreness of ℚ
sections.summary: IsNowhereDense.isMeagre (one-element countable union), isMeagre_singleton_real (closed + empty interior via interior_singleton), and isMeagre_rationals (ℚ = ⋃ q, {q} a countable union of meagre singletons).
sections.mathContext: In a space with no isolated points every singleton is nowhere dense; countable unions of meagre sets are meagre, so ℚ is meagre.

sections.title: ℚ Is Not a Gδ
sections.summary: not_isGδ_rationals: a dense Gδ is non-meagre (not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense), contradicting meagreness of ℚ. Restated for {x | ¬ Irrational x} (not_isGδ_setOf_not_irrational) and contrasted with isGδ_irrationals.
sections.mathContext: Dense + Gδ ⟹ residual ⟹ not meagre; ℚ is meagre, so ℚ is not Gδ.

sections.mathContext: {x | ContinuousAt f x} is Gδ; ℚ is not; hence they are never equal. The irrationals, being Gδ, are not obstructed.

conclusion.summary: The rationals ℚ ⊆ ℝ are not a Gδ set (not_isGδ_rationals): ℚ is dense, so a Gδ presentation would force it to be residual and non-meagre (not_isMeagre_of_isGδ_of_dense), but ℚ is meagre as a countable union of nowhere-dense singletons (isMeagre_rationals). Since the continuity set of any function is a Gδ (Mathlib's IsGδ.setOf_continuousAt), no f : ℝ → ℝ has continuity set equal to ℚ (continuitySet_ne_rationals, no_function_continuous_exactly_at_rationals): there is no function continuous at every rational and discontinuous at every irrational. The obstruction is one-sided — the irrationals are a Gδ (isGδ_irrationals), so they are not ruled out as a continuity set (irrationals_isGδ_no_obstruction). 127 lines, 11 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: This deploys the parent's meagre/residual dichotomy as a Gδ obstruction and reaches the classical impossibility theorem discussed alongside Thomae's function. The deep analytic half (continuity sets are Gδ) is delegated to Mathlib; the entry supplies the clean Baire obstruction on ℚ and the gluing step. The remaining direction — actually constructing Thomae's function continuous exactly at the irrationals — is recorded as a follow-up.
openQuestions: Construct Thomae's popcorn function and prove it is continuous exactly at the irrationals, realising the Gδ irrational side as a genuine continuity set.
Generalise: in any Baire space with no isolated points, a countable dense set is never a Gδ and hence never a continuity set.
